page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal SSD family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9254 processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, which provides 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present in this configuration.

In benchmark testing, this server demonstrates top-tier single-core and multi-core performance. It achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2272.0 and a multi-core score of 21196.0, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory performance is also highly competitive, with a PassMark memory score in the top 10% and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 296.64 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, which facilitate rapid software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-speed DDR5 memory, this bare metal configuration offers strong resource density and cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that require dedicated, non-virtualized hardware. It is highly suited for hosting large-scale databases, executing memory-intensive data processing pipelines, running local LLM inference for small to medium models, and managing high-throughput Redis deployments.
